config.theme: Sprint planning for a payments team at a fictional fintech
config.author: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code session)

cast.theme: Sprint planning for a payments team at a fictional fintech

personas.name: Hannah
personas.hidden_agenda: Her team's survey said meetings were the top complaint

personas.name: Ravi
personas.hidden_agenda: Embarrassed that the incident was in his code

personas.name: Chen
personas.goals: Ship card controls before the competitor does
personas.hidden_agenda: Leadership asked for card controls by name

personas.name: Lola
personas.hidden_agenda: Has six screens waiting and feels ignored

agenda.title: Incident follow-ups
agenda.goal: Close the action items from last week's top-up incident

agenda.title: Meeting load
agenda.goal: Decide what to cut from the team's meetings

facts.statement: Meeting hours per engineer per week = 9
Support contacts about top-ups per month = 1,150

beats.summary: The four open items from the incident; Ravi lowballs the failure rate
Reliability vs card controls; Chen's demand number is inflated
Sizing; a detour into Lola's pottery class
Meeting load; the hours number goes unchecked

turns.speaker: Hannah
turns.text: Morning. Let's start with the incident follow-ups. There are four still open.

turns.speaker: Ravi
turns.text: Two are mine. The retry logic and the alert on the bank callback.

turns.speaker: Hannah
turns.text: Where are they?

turns.speaker: Ravi
turns.text: The alert is done, it went in yesterday. The retry logic is half done.

turns.speaker: Chen
turns.text: And the failure rate's back to normal now, right? About one percent?

turns.speaker: Ravi
turns.text: Roughly, yes. It's settled down.

turns.speaker: Lola
turns.text: The other two items are the status banner and the support macro. Both were mine and Hannah's.

turns.speaker: Hannah
turns.text: The macro's done. The banner is waiting on design, which is, Lola, you.

turns.speaker: Lola
turns.text: It's one of six screens waiting for review. I keep asking for a slot.

turns.speaker: Hannah
turns.text: Then we'll give you a slot. That's on me.

turns.speaker: Lola
turns.text: Thank you.

turns.speaker: Chen
turns.text: It'd be good if someone wrote the incident up for the engineering blog.

turns.speaker: Hannah
turns.text: The big choice. Top-up reliability, or card controls.

turns.speaker: Chen
turns.text: Card controls. Over a thousand customers have asked for them. It's the most requested feature we have.

turns.speaker: Ravi
turns.text: Is it a thousand? I thought the request count was in the hundreds.

turns.speaker: Chen
turns.text: Let me check. Three hundred and forty. A thousand was all the feedback mentioning cards at all.

turns.speaker: Ravi
turns.text: Three forty. Meanwhile top-ups are eighteen thousand a day, and every failure is someone stuck at a till.

turns.speaker: Lola
turns.text: And support gets over a thousand contacts a month about top-ups.

turns.speaker: Chen
turns.text: Leadership asked for card controls by name.

turns.speaker: Hannah
turns.text: Leadership also asked why the rating dropped to four point one.

turns.speaker: Ravi
turns.text: I pulled the numbers this morning. I said one percent earlier, that was wrong. The failure rate is two point four.

turns.speaker: Chen
turns.text: Two point four. That's worse than I thought.

turns.speaker: Hannah
turns.text: Then reliability first. Card controls get a design spike so we're ready next sprint.

turns.speaker: Chen
turns.text: A spike. Fine. As long as it's real.

turns.speaker: Lola
turns.text: I'll do the card controls designs this sprint, if the review slot happens.

turns.speaker: Hannah
turns.text: Estimates. Ravi, the retry logic and the reliability work.

turns.speaker: Ravi
turns.text: Thirteen points for retries done properly, plus five for the bank timeout handling.

turns.speaker: Hannah
turns.text: We average twenty-six, with five engineers. That leaves room.

turns.speaker: Chen
turns.text: And the spike?

turns.speaker: Hannah
turns.text: Three points, time-boxed.

turns.speaker: Lola
turns.text: I finally finished my first bowl at the pottery class. It's lopsided, but it holds soup.

turns.speaker: Chen
turns.text: Pictures, or it didn't happen.

turns.speaker: Ravi
turns.text: My sister does pottery. She says the first fifty are all lopsided.

turns.speaker: Hannah
turns.text: Can we fit the banner and the design review backlog in too?

turns.speaker: Ravi
turns.text: The banner, yes. It's small once Lola's done.

turns.speaker: Hannah
turns.text: Okay, retries, timeout handling, the banner and the spike. That's the sprint.

turns.speaker: Chen
turns.text: Works for me.

turns.speaker: Hannah
turns.text: Last thing. The survey said meetings are the top complaint. We spend about five hours a week each in meetings.

turns.speaker: Ravi
turns.text: It feels like more.

turns.speaker: Chen
turns.text: Which ones can go?

turns.speaker: Lola
turns.text: The Wednesday sync. It repeats standup.

turns.speaker: Ravi
turns.text: And standup could be async two days a week.

turns.speaker: Chen
turns.text: I'd keep standup daily. Async means I find out about problems late.

turns.speaker: Hannah
turns.text: Then we cut the Wednesday sync and try async standup on Tuesdays and Thursdays for this sprint.

turns.speaker: Ravi
turns.text: Could we also protect Friday mornings? No meetings at all.

turns.speaker: Hannah
turns.text: Yes. I'll block Friday mornings on everyone's calendar today.

turns.speaker: Lola
turns.text: Who tells the other teams we've dropped the Wednesday sync? They join it sometimes.

turns.speaker: Chen
turns.text: The release train is on November fourteenth, so the retries need to be in by then.

turns.speaker: Ravi
turns.text: They'll be in. I'll have the retry logic in review by the eleventh.

turns.speaker: Hannah
turns.text: Good. Thanks, everyone.
